record_verbatim.objective: Confirm that FB2-SYS-SYR-000004's core claim is falsifiable against the pinned source: that the limit applied and the reaction reached are selected by the mode or direction rather than fixed. Two independent mechanisms in the source select on mode or direction. SOA_CheckTemperatures chooses between a discharge tier set and a charge tier set from the sign of the string current, so the same temperature passes or fails depending on direction. The application's state machine selects the contactor reaction from the item's own state and from the requests allowed in that state, and BMS_CheckStateRequest refuses an initialisation request outside the uninitialised state. Both are read from the pinned source and both can be falsified without running the item.

oracle_detail.residual_risk: Two mechanisms are checked that are not the one the requirement names. The requirement asks for reaction selected by mode; the source selects temperature limits by current direction and initialisation requests by state. Whether current direction is the reference project's notion of mode is an interpretation, and this record states the interpretation rather than hiding it.
oracle_detail.what_it_still_does_not_prove: It does not prove the reference project's reaction set per mode is the right set, that no mode is missing, or that the published mode reaches the vehicle control unit within the publication period the requirement also demands. The publication half of FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 is verified by a different mechanism and is not claimed here.
oracle_detail.what_the_oracle_is_not: It is not a measured reference: neither branch was exercised by a run in this authoring pass. It is not an analytical model: no timing or magnitude arithmetic is involved. It is not a synthetic assumption: the branching is in the source.
oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: The oracle is the branching the pinned source performs. The temperature path contains an explicit test of the current's sign that selects between two threshold sets, and the request path contains an explicit test of the current state that returns one of several distinct refusal values. Both are properties of code that exists, readable at the pinned commit, and falsifiable by changing one condition in either.

preconditions: The reference project's limit configuration is loaded.
The application's state machine is initialised in the uninitialised state.
record_verbatim.regression_selection: Re-run on every change to the temperature tier selection, to the request admissibility rules, to the application's state enumeration, or on any addition of a mode. Also re-run whenever a mode is added, because this measure can only check the modes the code actually branches on and a new mode is exactly the case it would miss.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.
